units.text: Groups of lines that differ in two or three of the input files are called ⟦0⟧diff3 hunks⟦1⟧, by analogy with ⟦2⟧ hunks (see ⟦3⟧Hunks⟦4⟧). If all three input files differ in a ⟦5⟧ hunk, the hunk is called a ⟦6⟧three-way hunk⟦7⟧; if just two input files differ, it is a ⟦8⟧two-way hunk⟦9⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Groups of lines that differ in two or three of the input files are called diff3 hunks, by analogy with diff hunks (see Hunks). If all three input files differ in a diff3 hunk, the hunk is called a three-way hunk; if just two input files differ, it is a two-way hunk.

units.text: As with ⟦0⟧, several solutions are possible. When comparing the files ‘⟦1⟧’, ‘⟦2⟧’, and ‘⟦3⟧’, ⟦4⟧ normally finds ⟦5⟧ hunks by merging the two-way hunks output by the two commands ‘⟦6⟧’ and ‘⟦7⟧’. This does not necessarily minimize the size of the output, but exceptions should be rare.
units.sourceHTML: As with diff, several solutions are possible. When comparing the files ‘A’, ‘B’, and ‘C’, diff3 normally finds diff3 hunks by merging the two-way hunks output by the two commands ‘diff A B’ and ‘diff A C’. This does not necessarily minimize the size of the output, but exceptions should be rare.
